title: Company-wide policies and processes: Access & Permissions, Change Management, Data Management, Procurement & Expenses, Vendor Management, Travel Policies, and Internal Templates
author: Avery Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and process templates for the following areas: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended as the single source of truth for employees, team leads, and approvers.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all Redwood employees, contractors with network or data access, and vendors under contract.
Exclusions: project-level SOPs that live in team wiki pages; product feature design docs.

Owners and escalation
---------------------
- Primary owner: People Ops (policy maintenance and company-wide approvals).
- Security owner: Security & Compliance (access controls, RBAC, IAM reviews).
- Finance owner: Finance & Legal (procurement, expenses, vendor contracts).
- Operational contacts: listed within each section.

1) Access & Permissions
------------------------
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access across products, cloud accounts, internal tools, and physical spaces.

Key principles:
- Least privilege by default: grant the minimum role required for the task.
- Role-based access where possible; use groups instead of individual grants.
- Time-bound access for short-lived tasks (use access expiration).
- Multi-factor authentication (MFA) required for all accounts with privileged access.

Process: Request -> Approval -> Provisioning -> Review
1. Request: Employee opens an access request using the Access Request form (HRIS / Okta integration).
2. Approver: Direct manager + resource owner (service owner or team lead) must approve.
3. Provisioning: Security team or automated provisioning system (Okta/SCIM) applies role.
4. Validation: Requester confirms access works within 24 hours.
5. Review: Quarterly access review initiated by Security; owners must attest.

Standard roles & thresholds:
- Admin (full org level): restricted to ~5 people; requires executive approval + Security sign-off.
- Service Maintainer: granted per-service, requires owner approval.
- Read-only: broadly available where safe (e.g., metrics dashboards).

Emergency access (break-glass):
- Use the break-glass request channel documented in the Incident Response playbook. All break-glass grants are time-limited (max 8 hours) and require post-incident justification and audit.

2) Change Management
---------------------
Objective: Controlled, auditable changes to production and infra services to reduce incidents and enable quick rollbacks.

Change types:
- Standard change: pre-approved, low-risk (e.g., routine config tweak).
- Normal change: requires CAB review for changes that affect multiple services or have moderate risk.
- Emergency change: used for urgent fixes; must be retrospectively reviewed.

Change workflow:
1. Submit change in Change Tracker (Jira ticket with change type, rollback plan, owner, and scheduled window).
2. Automated tests and staging validation required for any code or infra change.
3. CAB (Change Advisory Board) review for Normal changes: weekly meeting; attendees include representatives from Eng, SRE, Security, and Product.
4. Approval: Changes are approved via the Jira workflow.
5. Implementation: Follow the runbook/implementation checklist.
6. Post-change verification: Verify SLOs & metrics for 30 minutes (or longer for higher-risk changes).
7. Postmortem: For all Emergency changes and any Normal change that adversely affected production.

Rollback criteria: Pre-defined in the change ticket; if error rate > 2% above baseline or latency SLO breach > 20% during verification, initiate rollback.

3) Data Management
------------------
Goal: Protect customer and company data while enabling teams to work productively.

Data classification:
- Public: safe for public disclosure.
- Internal: company-internal, not customer-sensitive.
- Confidential: PII, customer data, model training sets, and other regulated data.
- Restricted: cryptographic keys, full backups, and other high-impact assets.

Handling rules by classification:
- Confidential & Restricted: encrypted at rest and in transit, access via RBAC only, KMS usage required for keys, logging enabled.
- Internal: stored in company-managed systems with standard access controls.
- Public: no special controls required, but marketing must approve external release.

Data lifecycle & retention:
- Retention baselines: customer logs 90 days, metrics 13 months, backups 90 days (or customer-specified).
- Deletion/erasure: follow the Data Erasure request process in the Security & Compliance space.

Data sharing & exports:
1. Data export request: open Data Export ticket with purpose, dataset description, recipients, and retention plan.
2. Approval: Data owner + Security must approve exports containing Confidential or Restricted data.
3. Delivery: Use approved transfer methods (S3 with signed URLs + encryption).

Audit & monitoring:
- Sensitive dataset accesses are logged and reviewed monthly.
- Anomalous export alerts trigger an immediate audit.

4) Procurement & Expenses
-------------------------
Purpose: Fiscal stewardship and consistent purchasing experience.

Spending thresholds & approvals:
- < $1,000: Manager approval.
- $1,000 - $25,000: Department head + Finance purchase order (PO).
- > $25,000: VP-level approval + Finance + Legal review (contracts + SOW).

Procurement workflow:
1. Request: Employee creates a Purchase Request in Procurement Portal (include justification, vendor, cost center, and budget code).
2. Finance reviews for budget and vendor history.
3. Legal reviews contracts for > $10,000 or when vendor requires unique T&Cs.
4. PO issuance and purchase.
5. Receipt & reconciliation: submit receipts within 30 days (use expense system).

Expense policy highlights:
- Reimbursable items: travel, client meals (per diem limits), approved equipment, training.
- Non-reimbursable: personal expenses, fines, alcohol without business justification.
- Card usage: company cards issued for engineering and other teams per policy; reconcile monthly.

Travel approvals:
- Domestic travel: manager approval.
- International travel: manager + People Ops approval for visas/insurance.
- All travel must follow the Travel Policy section below.

5) Vendor Management
--------------------
Objective: Ensure risks and obligations with third parties are managed consistently.

Vendor lifecycle stages:
- Onboarding: risk assessment, security questionnaire (SIG/CAIQ), contract, and PO.
- Monitoring: quarterly health checks, usage reviews, and invoices.
- Offboarding: revoke access, return or destroy data, and archive contracts.

Onboarding checklist:
1. Vendor Risk Assessment (Finance & Security): sensitivity of data, access needed, geographic constraints.
2. Security Questionnaire: vendor completes SIG/standard questionnaire.
3. Legal review: contract, SLA, indemnities, data processing agreement (DPA) where applicable.
4. Procurement: PO and payment terms finalized.
5. Provisioning: least-privilege access only; logs enabled.

SLA & performance tracking:
- All vendors with access to production services or customer data must have an SLA or documented support expectations.
- Vendor performance is reviewed semi-annually; failures trigger escalation to Legal & Procurement.

6) Travel Policy (high-level)
-----------------------------
Principles: safe, cost-effective, compliant with local laws, and aligned with business needs.

Booking & class of service:
- Domestic flights < 4 hours: economy.
- Domestic flights > 4 hours and international flights: premium economy or business with manager approval.
- Hotels: mid-range business hotels; use preferred vendor rates when available.

Per diem & meals:
- Reasonable meal reimbursement up to published per-diem (refer to country-specific table below). Receipt required for meals > $75.

Health & safety:
- International travelers: register trip with People Ops, ensure travel insurance is valid, and complete pre-travel security briefing for high-risk destinations.

Expense submission:
- Submit travel expenses in the Expense System within 14 days of trip completion with receipts and purpose.

7) Internal Templates & Examples
-------------------------------
Included templates (available in the Templates library):
- Access Request form (Okta request): fields, approvers, example justification text.
- Change Request ticket template (Jira): fields for rollback plan, verification steps, and CAB notes.
- Data Export request template: purpose, dataset, retention, approvers.
- Purchase Request form: vendor, justification, budget code, approver path.
- Vendor Onboarding checklist: required documents and timeline estimates.
- Travel pre-approval template: trip justification, itinerary, insurance info.

Template usage guidance:
- Always copy the template header and maintain versioning (e.g., template-v1.2).
- Attach supporting artifacts (screenshots, diagrams, vendor quotes) to the ticket.

B. Quick reference tables

| ---- | ---------------- | ---------- | ----------- |
| Access requests | Manager + Service owner | Security (24h) | Provisioned within 48h |
| Procurement < $1k | Manager | Finance (3 days) | PO / Approval within 3 business days |

C. Change definition examples
- Standard: Updating a monitoring threshold.
- Normal: Schema migration that touches multiple services.
- Emergency: Hotfix for production outage.

How to propose changes to this document
-------------------------------------
1. Create a Confluence edit proposal, tagging People Ops and Security.
2. For material changes (policy or threshold changes), submit a formal proposal and schedule a review with People Ops + Finance + Security.
3. Minor edits (clarifications, typos) can be merged by People Ops with one reviewer.
